thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: reserved-pool-resv-east-1a utilization = 99%. queue length for reserved tenants > 1200, median token latency spiking. top offender: tenant=nov ahealth (reserved_id=rsv-907). autoscaler reported 429s from cloud API when requesting new instances.
anya (oncall): paging in. I'm taking first responder.
marcus (sre): on it, pulling pool metrics. is the autoscaler failing or cloud-side throttling?
devin (runtime): autoscaler returned: 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED from provider. request id abc-987. we retried 2x then backoff.
anya (oncall): thanks. impact: are customer sessions dropping or just queued?
sarah (cs): NovaHealth is seeing user errors — they reported failed inferences for some jobs, support ticket open. They have high-priority reserved capacity.
raj (mlops): checked reservation mapping: rsv-907 pinned to resv-east-1a (4 x A100). current active containers = 4, queued tasks = 1900 across their workers. preemptible pool already at 80%.
marcus (sre): queues growing since 07:12 UTC. autoscaler logs show repeated 429s starting 07:16. our scale window exhausted retries.
ops-lead: quick options: 1) Manually provision emergency nodes (need cloud-ops uplift) 2) Evict low-priority sessions in reserved pool to free GPUs 3) Failover tenant to another region/pool if cross-region replication exists.
anya (oncall): do we have a fast path to free GPU memory by evicting ephemeral / best-effort jobs in this pool?
devin (runtime): yes — we have eviction tag "best-effort" on non-reserved sessions. can run "/evict --pool resv-east-1a --tag best-effort --min-free 1". will that be safe for NovaHealth?
marcus (sre): evicting best-effort should free ~1-2 GPUs worth of headroom quickly. but NovaHealth reserved sessions still may be saturated depending on pinned slots.
anya (oncall): do it. devin, run eviction. log output here.
devin (runtime): running now. paste: ```
$ radmin evict --pool resv-east-1a --tag best-effort --min-free 2
Evicted 38 sessions. Freed ~1.8 GPU equivalents.```
marcus (sre): saw freed capacity. queue length dropped ~270. token latency improved slightly. still above target for NovaHealth (they're still experiencing 503s).
anya (oncall): can we short-term route NovaHealth traffic to a compatible variant in resv-west-2 while we scale? compatibility check: model = redwood-open-13b-8q. available variant in west: redwood-open-13b-8q-int8, compatible for inference but may have small perf delta.
devin (runtime): routing policy requires customer opt-in for cross-region due to data residency. NovaHealth hasn't opted in. we need CS + legal signoff for cross-region — not fast.
sarah (cs): I'm live with NovaHealth contact. They are under heavy load and prefer we prioritize uptime over strict locality for now. I have verbal go-ahead to failover if needed, but will confirm in ticket.
ops-lead: given autoscaler hitting rate limits, we should also attempt manual provisioning while CS confirms failover OK. marcus, can you open a cloud support ticket to lift the rate limit or request emergency capacity?
marcus (sre): opening ticket now with cloud provider, referencing request abc-987 and quota escalate. ETA unknown. also kicking off manual provisioning for 2x emergency VMs (will take ~6-9 minutes).
raj (mlops): initiating manual node bootstrap with preloaded runtime image to minimize startup. I'm also enabling aggressive KV cache eviction for NovaHealth to reduce memory pressure: ```
curl -X POST https://orchestration/internal/pools/resv-east-1a/cache-evict -d '{"tenant":"rsv-907","pct":35}'
```
anya (oncall): good. track timings. we'll also put a soft throttle on non-reserved burst traffic to preserve tokens for reserved tenants. set token bucket for shared tier to 50% of normal for 10m.
devin (runtime): applied throttling: "shared-tier" rate limit -> 50% for 10m. ruleset id rt-564.
marcus (sre): manual nodes are provisioning. cloud console shows two new instances initializing at 07:27 UTC.
sarah (cs): NovaHealth confirms they see partial recovery now but still some queued jobs. they're asking whether this will be an ongoing issue or a one-off surge.
ops-lead: root cause likely a rapid influx of long-running sessions from NovaHealth + autoscaler API rate limiting. mitigation steps: evict best-effort, throttle shared, manual bootstrap, request cloud quota bump, and CS approval for cross-region failover as contingency.
anya (oncall): update incident status: severity -> Sev2 (enterprise impact, customer-facing degradation). I'm assigning follow-ups: marcus -> cloud escalation and infra follow-through; devin -> confirm eviction logs + monitor runtime; raj -> ensure cache eviction completed; sarah -> keep customer posted and confirm cross-region opt-in; ops-lead -> coordinate postmortem.
marcus (sre): cloud ticket created: TKT-7802. included logs and request for emergency capacity.
devin (runtime): eviction logs: ```
[07:25:13] evict: sess-1234 freed
[07:25:14] evict: sess-1268 freed
... total 38 sessions
```
raj (mlops): cache-evict responded 200 OK, TTL reduce applied. memory pressure metrics show 22% drop.
anya (oncall): manual nodes now ready and joined cluster at 07:33 UTC. autoscaler still throttling but we have immediate capacity. latency normalized for reserved tenant over last 2m.
sarah (cs): passing message to NovaHealth: "We provisioned emergency capacity and applied mitigations; we're monitoring. CS will follow up with dedicated post-incident summary and options for reservation sizing or burst add-on"
ops-lead: good. keep this thread updated. we'll run a quick blameless timeline tomorrow. add action: increase autoscaler retry/backoff logic and surface cloud API quota metrics to monitoring.
marcus (sre): noted. creating follow-up ticket ENG-1423 for autoscaler robustness and ENG-1424 for quota dashboards.
anya (oncall): closing active pager for now — transitioning to incident review mode. will update when postmortem is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
